sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: UPPER LOW OVER SRN ALBERTA WILL MOVE SEWD TO NEAR THE U.S.-CANADIAN BORDER BY 26/12Z RESULTING IN STRONGER WLY MID-LEVEL FLOW FROM THE UPPER MIDWEST EWD INTO NEW ENGLAND. UPPER LEVEL HIGH PRESSURE AREAS WILL BECOME ESTABLISHED OVER BOTH THE SOUTHWEST AND SOUTHEAST U.S. SURFACE LOW PRESSURE WILL MOVE EAST ACROSS THE UPPER MS VALLEY/GREAT LAKES WHILE A TRAILING COLD FRONT MOVES INTO THE CENTRAL/SRN HIGH PLAINS. A WARM FRONT WILL MOVE NEWD ACROSS THE MIDWEST AND GREAT LAKES AND THEN EXTEND SEWD INTO THE CAROLINAS.

sections.title: CENTRAL PLAINS/UPPER MIDWEST EAST ACROSS THE GREAT LAKES
sections.text: AN MCS WITH STG/SVR TSTMS WILL LIKELY BE ON GOING AT 12Z WED ACROSS PORTIONS OF MN/WI/UPPER MI DRIVEN BY ISENTROPIC LIFT ASSOCIATED WITH A MODERATELY STRONG LOW-LEVEL JET. THIS COMPLEX MAY WEAKEN SOMEWHAT DURING THE MORNING...HOWEVER RESIDUAL CLOUDS AND OUTFLOW SHOULD REINFORCE THE WARM FRONT ACROSS THE GREAT LAKES REGION. INTENSE DAYTIME HEATING WILL RESULT IN A VERY UNSTABLE BUT CAPPED AIR MASS IN THE WARM SECTOR UNTIL LATE AFTN. AS HEIGHT FALLS OVERSPREAD THE AREA SVR TSTMS WILL LIKELY DEVELOP/RE-INTENSIFY NEAR THE WARM FRONT. SUPERCELLS MAY INITIALLY DEVELOP WITH A THREAT OF LARGE HAIL/DAMAGING WINDS. A TORNADO THREAT MAY EXIST WITH ANY DISCRETE STORM IN THE VICINITY OF THE WARM FRONT. WITH TIME UPSCALE GROWTH INTO AN MCS APPEARS LIKELY WITH A CONTINUED SVR WIND/HAIL THREAT EWD INTO WRN NY LATE WED NIGHT. TSTM DEVELOPMENT SWWD ALONG THE COLD FRONT IS EXPECTED BY LATE AFTN/EARLY EVENING IN A MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS WITH LARGE DCAPE IN THE RANGE OF 1000-1500 J/KG. STRONG WIND GUSTS WILL BE THE PRIMARY THREAT WITH ISOLATED LARGE HAIL ALSO POSSIBLE. A SECONDARY COLD FRONT ASSOCIATED WITH THE ALBERTA UPPER LOW WILL MOVE ACROSS NRN MN WITH ISOLATED STG/SVR STORMS POSSIBLE.

sections.title: CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: LOW-LEVEL POST-FRONTAL UPSLOPE FLOW SHOULD RESULT IN ISOLATED TO WIDELY SCTD TSTMS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING STG WIND GUSTS AND HAIL.

sections.title: TN/OH/VALLEY AND SOUTHEAST U.S
sections.text: GUIDANCE IS CONSISTENT IN DEVELOPING TSTMS ALONG AND SOUTH OF THE SURFACE FRONT IN AN ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY MOD-STG INSTABILITY AND SUFFICIENT 0-6 KM SHEAR TO SUPPORT A MIX OF PULSE-TYPE AND MULTICELL CLUSTERS. STRONG DOWNBURST WINDS WILL BE THE PRIMARY THREAT. ..BUNTING/LEITMAN.. 07/25/2012

sections.title: MID-UPPER MS VALLEY TO THE GREAT LAKES THROUGH TONIGHT
sections.text: A MIDLEVEL TROUGH OVER SK THIS MORNING WILL PROGRESS SEWD TO NW MN BY EARLY THURSDAY. THIS PRIMARY TROUGH WILL BE PRECEDED BY EMBEDDED SPEED MAXIMA/REMNANT MCV/S FROM THE NRN PLAINS TO THE UPPER GREAT LAKES. AT THE SURFACE...A CYCLONE NEAR THE SD/MN BORDER AS OF 12Z WILL TRANSLATE EWD ACROSS SRN MN TO CENTRAL WI BY THIS EVENING...REACHING NRN LOWER MI OVERNIGHT. MEANWHILE...A SURFACE WARM FRONT WILL MOVE NEWD ACROSS WI/IL/LOWER MI/INDIANA IN ADVANCE OF THE CYCLONE...AND A TRAILING COLD FRONT WILL MOVE SEWD ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS AND MID MS VALLEY BY TONIGHT. THE RICHEST BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE /DEWPOINTS IN THE LOW 70S/ WILL REMAIN ON THE IMMEDIATE COOL SIDE OF THE WARM FRONT...WHILE A HOT/DEEPLY-MIXED AIR MASS SPREADS NEWD ACROSS THE MID MS VALLEY TOWARD LAKE MI BY AFTERNOON. A LARGE CLUSTER OF ELEVATED CONVECTION IS ONGOING INVOF WRN LAKE SUPERIOR...AIDED BY LOW-LEVEL WAA AND AN INFLUX OF RICHER MOISTURE FROM THE SW. THIS REGIME WILL PERSIST THROUGH LATE MORNING ACROSS NRN WI/UPPER MI WITH A MARGINAL RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS/HAIL...AND THEN OVERSPREAD NRN LOWER MI THIS AFTERNOON. NEWD PROGRESSION OF THE WARM FRONT AND SURFACE HEATING COULD RESULT IN ADDITIONAL THUNDERSTORM DEVE

sections.title: NW MN THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: ISOLATED STRONG/SEVERE STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING ALONG A SECONDARY WEAK FRONTAL SURGE...IMMEDIATELY IN ADVANCE OF THE SK-MB MIDLEVEL TROUGH. AFTER MORNING CLOUD DEBRIS CLEARS...RESIDUAL BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE MID 60S WILL COMBINE WITH DAYTIME HEATING TO SUPPORT MLCAPE NEAR 1500 J/KG ACROSS N/NW MN. THE MODERATE INSTABILITY AND EFFECTIVE-BULK SHEAR OF 30-40 KT COULD SUPPORT A FEW ORGANIZED STORMS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING DAMAGING GUSTS AND LARGE HAIL.

sections.title: SC/GA THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING
sections.text: AN MCV AND WEAKENING THUNDERSTORM CLUSTER ARE MOVING SEWD FROM WRN NC TOWARD SC. SURFACE HEATING AND RICHER LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE S-SW OF THE OUTFLOW ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CONVECTION WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF MLCAPE VALUES OF 2500-3500 J/KG. THUS...ADDITIONAL THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED BY MIDDAY-EARLY AFTERNOON ACROSS SC/GA...BOTH ALONG THE DIFFERENTIAL HEATING ZONE/REMNANT OUTFLOW AND ALONG THE ATLANTIC COAST SEA BREEZE. THOUGH VERTICAL SHEAR WILL BE WEAK...THERMODYNAMIC PROFILES WILL FAVOR STRONG DOWNBURSTS WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR AT LEAST ISOLATED DAMAGING WINDS THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING. ..THOMPSON/MOSIER.. 07/25/2012

sections.title: MID-UPR MS VLY TO THE GRTLKS
sections.text: STACKED SK UPR LOW WILL MOVE ALONG THE INTERNATIONAL BORDER TO LAKE OF THE WOODS BY 12Z. PRECEDING BELT OF MID-LVL FLOW WILL CARRY EMBEDDED REMNANT MCV/S FROM THE CNTRL/NRN PLNS EWD INTO THE CNTRL GRTLKS REGION THROUGH TONIGHT. MEANWHILE...A 1002 MB LOW OVER SWRN MN AT 16Z WILL REACH NRN LWR MI LATER TONIGHT. WRMFNT DEVELOPING ACROSS THE UPR MIDWEST NOW WILL TRANSLATE INTO THE CNTRL GRTLKS TONIGHT WITH A TRAILING CDFNT MOVING SEWD ACROSS THE CNTRL PLNS AND MID MS VLY. FCST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST THAT THE MORE ROBUST BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE...CHARACTERIZED BY LWR 70S SFC DEW POINTS...WILL REMAIN ALONG THE IMMEDIATE COOL SIDE OF THE WRM FRONTAL ZONE WITH A HOT/DEEPLY-MIXED AIR MASS SPREADING NEWD FROM THE CNTRL PLNS INTO THE MID-MS VLY/LK MI THIS AFTN. A WEAKENING ELEVATED MCS CONTINUES TO MOVE ACROSS THE UPR GRTLKS AT 16Z...THRIVING ON MOISTURE/WARM ADVECTION DEVELOPING QUICKLY NEWD. ATTENTION WILL TURN TO SFC-BASED TSTMS EXPECTED TO DEVELOP LATER THIS AFTN/EVE ALONG SRN FRINGES OF CURRENT ACTIVITY AND IMMEDIATELY AHEAD OF THE SFC LOW/CDFNT FROM NRN LK MI SWWD TO CNTRL NEB WHERE VSB SATL INDICATES CONSIDERABLE ACCAS ALREADY PRESENT. WLY DEEP-LAYER SHEAR OF 35+ KTS WILL FAVOR INITIAL SUPE

sections.title: NRN MN
sections.text: SECONDARY FRONTAL SURGE ALONG SRN PERIPHERY OF STACKED SK LOW WILL MOVE EWD THROUGH THE RED RVR VLY AND INTO NRN MN THIS AFTN/EVE. AFTER LOW CLOUDS DISSOLVE...MID/UPR 60S SFC DEW POINTS BENEATH COOLING MID-LVL TEMPS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO MLCAPES TO 1500 J/KG AHEAD OF THE FRONT. WDLY SCTD TSTMS WILL DEVELOP 19-21Z OVER ERN ND AND PROGRESS ACROSS NRN MN THROUGH EVE. WLY DEEP-LAYER SHEAR OF 30-40 KTS WILL SUPPORT SUPERCELLS WITH DMGG WIND GUSTS AND LARGE HAIL. ACTIVITY WILL MOVE INTO PARTS OF CNTRL/ERN MN BY 12Z...BUT THE SVR THREATS SHOULD WANE AFTER SUNSET.

sections.title: CNTRL/SRN GA AND THE FL PNHDL
sections.text: UPDATE HAS INCLUDED AN UPGRADE TO A LOW-END SLGT RISK FOR A FEW DMGG MICROBURSTS ACROSS THE REGION FROM MID-AFTN INTO THE EARLY EVE. VSB SATL SHOWS EVIDENCE OF AN MCV THAT WILL TRANSLATE SWD FROM CNTRL SC INTO PARTS OF CNTRL/SRN GA THIS AFTN. THIS WILL LIKELY ENHANCE DIURNAL CONVECTION THAT DEVELOPS ALONG PRE-EXISTING BOUNDARIES AND THE SEABREEZE CIRCULATIONS. ALTHOUGH VERTICAL SHEAR WILL BE WEAK...PRESENCE OF VERY STEEP LLVL LAPSE RATES WILL BE FAVORABLE FOR PULSE MULTICELLS WITH STRONG MICROBURSTS...SOME OF WHICH MAY PRODUCE DMG. ACTIVITY WILL DIMINISH AFTER SUNSET.

sections.title: OH VLY
sections.text: LATEST HRRR RUNS ARE ROBUST IN DEVELOPING TSTMS IN THE OH VLY ALONG THE RETREATING WRMFNT. OTHER CONVECTION-PERMITTING MODELS ARE LESS ROBUST AND ARE PREFERRED IN THE REGION WHERE SHORT-WAVE RIDGING IS EXPECTED TODAY. AN ISOLD SVR TSTM /DMGG WINDS AND HAIL/ CANNOT BE RULED OUT WITHIN THE DVLPG CU FIELD IN PARTS OF SRN IND...SRN OH AND CNTRL/ERN KY. BUT...WIDESPREAD SVR STORMS ARE NOT EXPECTED. ..RACY/COHEN.. 07/25/2012

sections.title: MID-UPR MS VLY TO THE GRTLKS
sections.text: MAIN ADJUSTMENT WAS TO ADD A SIGNIFICANT WIND AREA TO PARTS OF ERN WI TO CNTRL LOWER MI. TSTMS SHOULD FORM IN PARTS OF CNTRL WI WHERE THE PERIPHERY OF HOTTEST SURFACE TEMPERATURES INTERSECTS THE COLD FRONT PUSHING SEWD ACROSS THE REGION. HOWEVER...SOME UNCERTAINTY DOES EXIST IN THIS SCENARIO OCCURRING OWING TO THE DEGREE OF CAPPING DEPICTED IN ACARS DATA INVOF MSP AND VEERED WIND PROFILE IN MOST OF THE WARM SECTOR. BUT...SHOULD ACTIVITY FORM /AS DEPICTED IN MANY CONVECTION-ALLOWING MODELS/...COMBINATION OF CAPE/SHEAR WILL BE RATHER FAVORABLE FOR UPSCALE GROWTH AND BOW ECHOES THIS EVENING. ENHANCED SLIGHT RISK PROBABILITIES APPEAR APPROPRIATE THIS OUTLOOK. THE ERN EXTENT OF THE THREAT INTO THE LOWER GREAT LAKES WILL REQUIRE SUBSTANTIAL DESTABILIZATION GIVEN WARM FRONT STILL BACK IN NERN IND TO SWRN OH.

sections.title: NRN MN
sections.text: NO CHANGES NEEDED. SEE MCD 1584 FOR ADDITIONAL DISCUSSION.

sections.title: SOUTHEAST
sections.text: PRIMARY TSTM DEVELOPMENT SHOULD REMAIN OVER PARTS OF THE SRN APPALACHIANS TOWARDS THE FL PANHANDLE/SRN GA...WITH PULSE TO LOOSELY ORGANIZED MULTICELLS CAPABLE OF LOCALIZED MICROBURSTS/MARGINAL HAIL. SEE MCDS 1583 AND 1585 FOR A MORE THOROUGH DISCUSSION OF THIS REGION. ..GRAMS.. 07/25/2012 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1128 AM CDT WED JUL 25 2012/

sections.title: GREAT LAKES AREA
sections.text: EARLY THIS EVENING A COLD FRONT EXTENDS FROM A SFC LOW IN NERN WI SWWD THROUGH CNTRL AND SWRN WI...IA AND THE CNTRL PLAINS. A WARM FRONT STRETCHES SEWD FROM THE LOW THROUGH LAKE MI...NERN IND AND SWRN OH. A RESERVOIR OF STRONG INSTABILITY /2500-3000 J/KG MLCAPE/ EXISTS IN WARM SECTOR FROM NRN IL...SRN AND CNTRL WI THROUGH SWRN LOWER MI AND INTO A PORTION OF THE OH VALLEY. STORMS HAVE INITIATED NEAR THE TRIPLE POINT IN NERN WI AS WELL AS FARTHER EAST WITHIN ZONE OF WARM ADVECTION AND ISENTROPIC LIFT NORTH OF THE WARM FRONT ACROSS NRN LOWER MI. A BELT OF STRONG DEEP LAYER FLOW AND 50 KT SWLY LLJ IN ASSOCIATION WITH A PROGRESSIVE MID LEVEL SPEED MAX WILL SHIFT EWD THROUGH THE GREAT LAKES THIS EVENING AND TONIGHT SUPPORTING 40-50 KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR FAVORABLE FOR ORGANIZED SEVERE STORMS. POTENTIAL EXISTS FOR A FEW SUPERCELLS WITH INITIAL STORMS. HOWEVER...ACTIVITY WILL LIKELY GROW UPSCALE INTO AN ORGANIZED CLUSTER/MCS WITH BOWING SEGMENTS CAPABLE OF WIDESPREAD DAMAGING WIND THROUGH PARTS OF CNTRL LOWER MI...EVENTUALLY INTO WRN NY LATER TONIGHT.

sections.title: CNTRL PLAINS THROUGH UPPER MS VALLEY AREA
sections.text: STORMS CONTINUE DEVELOPING ALONG AND AHEAD OF NE-SW ORIENTED FRONT FROM IA SWWD INTO KS. ACTIVITY IS EMBEDDED WITHIN MODEST VERTICAL SHEAR SUPPORTIVE OF MULTICELLS...BUT THE THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT WITH STEEP LAPSE RATES AND MODERATE INSTABILITY WILL CONTINUE TO PROMOTE A THREAT OF ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND AS STORMS DEVELOP EWD NEXT FEW HOURS. A GRADUAL DECREASE IN INTENSITY IS EXPECTED LATER THIS EVENING AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER STABILIZES. ..DIAL.. 07/26/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: PULSE-TYPE STORMS MAY POSE A LOCALIZED SVR THREAT THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. GIVEN THE DISORGANIZED NATURE OF THE CONVECTION...AND THE SPORADIC NATURE OF ANY SVR STORMS...A WW IS NOT NEEDED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AMIDST A MOIST AIR MASS CHARACTERIZED BY PW OF 1.75-2.00 INCHES PER GPS DATA...STRONG DIURNAL HEATING WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT DESTABILIZATION. MODIFIED 12Z OBSERVED SOUNDINGS SUGGEST THAT MLCAPE VALUES OF 2500-3500 J/KG WILL BE COMMON ACROSS THE AREA THROUGH THE MID/LATE AFTERNOON. WITH LITTLE/NO INHIBITION...CONVECTION WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP/INTENSIFY FROM A VARIETY OF SOURCES: /1/ DEVELOPING SEA BREEZE CONVERGENCE ZONES OVER INLAND AREAS ADJACENT TO THE GULF/ATLANTIC WATERS... /2/ A FIELD OF ENHANCED BOUNDARY-LAYER CUMULUS EXTENDING FROM FAR SERN AL INTO SWRN/S-CNTRL GA AND PARTS OF THE FL PANHANDLE -- I.E. ACROSS THE WARM SIDE OF A DIFFERENTIAL HEATING ZONE PERIPHERAL TO A HIGH-CLOUD SHIELD ACCOMPANYING CLUSTERS OF CONVECTION OVER THE OFFSHORE WATERS OF THE NERN GULF... /3/ NEAR AND JUST SW OF A STALLED FRONT ARCING FROM SWRN NC INTO NERN GA AND FAR SRN SC...AND /4/ CUMULUS-CONVERGENCE LINES WITHIN THE UNSTABLE SECTOR SW OF THE FRONT. GIVEN THE AFOREMENTIONED DEGREE OF BUOYANCY...VIGOROUS UPDRAFTS/DOWNDRAFTS ARE ANTICIPATED WITH CONVECTION THIS AFTERNOON. SPORADIC INSTANCES OF DMGG WIND GUSTS AND MARGINALLY SVR HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE. HOWEVER...WITH AOB 15 KT OF FLOW EVIDENT BELOW THE 4-KM AGL LEVEL PER AREA VWP DATA...WEAK LOW/MID-LEVEL FLOW WILL FOSTER A PULSE/DISORGANIZED CONVECTIVE MODE. ANY INSTANCES OF SVR STORMS SHOULD REMAIN ISOLATED/SPORADIC.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AT LEAST ISOLATED STORMS ARE LIKELY TO FORM OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS WITH HAIL THE MAIN SEVERE THREAT. UNCERTAINTY IN TERMS OF STORM COVERAGE MAY PRECLUDE A WATCH.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SURFACE ANALYSIS SHOWS A TROUGH FROM SRN MANITOBA SEWD ACROSS MN...WITH NWLY SURFACE WINDS INCREASE IN A POST FRONTAL REGIME TO THE W. NEAR THE SFC TROUGH...DEWPOINTS WERE HOLDING NEAR 70 F...WHICH WAS RESULTING IN MUCAPE IN EXCESS OF 2000 J/KG. VISIBLE IMAGERY SHOWS A LINE OF CU SHARPENING ALONG THE SECONDARY WIND SHIFT/FRONTAL SURGE FROM ERN ND INTO N CNTRL SD. GRADUAL HEIGHT FALLS AND COOLING ALOFT WILL PERSIST THIS AFTERNOON...AND THE SFC TROUGH WILL SLOWLY MOVE E. WITH CONTINUED DESTABILIZATION FROM HEATING...AT LEAST ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS WITH LARGE HAIL ARE EXPECTED TO FORM. LONG STRAIGHT HODOGRAPHS MAY FAVOR SPLITTING CELLS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED SVR THREAT WILL EXIST THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. WHILE CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED...THE ISSUANCE OF A WW IS CURRENTLY UNLIKELY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AMIDST POCKETS OF DIURNAL HEADING WITHIN THE MOIST SIDE OF A PW GRADIENT ZONE LYING FROM THE OH VALLEY TO THE CAROLINAS...DESTABILIZATION IS UNDERWAY ACROSS PARTS OF THE CNTRL/SRN APPALACHIANS. MLCAPE VALUES OF 1500-2500 J/KG ARE COMMON ACROSS MUCH OF THE AREA -- HIGHEST ON THE WARM SIDE OF A CONVECTIVELY REINFORCED BOUNDARY -- PER MODIFIED 12Z OBSERVED SOUNDINGS. OROGRAPHIC ASCENT WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT AN UPTICK IN CUMULUS DEVELOPMENT AND ISOLATED TO WIDELY SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. THE AFOREMENTIONED BUOYANCY MAY YIELD STRONG UPDRAFTS/DOWNDRAFTS...WITH THE STRONGEST STORMS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING MARGINALLY SVR WIND GUSTS AND PERHAPS MARGINALLY SVR HAIL. WITH THE PRIMARY ZONE OF STRONGER NWLYS REMAINING N OF THE AREA...STORM ORGANIZATION IS EXPECTED TO BE GENERALLY LACKING. HOWEVER...A LOCALIZED ZONE OF ENHANCED -- I.E. AROUND 30-35 KT -- NLY FLOW EXISTS WITHIN THE 3.5-4.5-KM-AGL LAYER PER AREA VWP DATA...PERHAPS IN ASSOCIATION WITH A REMNANT MCV/PERTURBATION. IF THIS FLOW IS ABLE TO BE MAINTAINED...A FEW MULTICELL CLUSTERS MAY EVOLVE WITH RELATIVELY HIGHER CHANCES FOR PRODUCING DMGG WIND GUSTS. REGARDLESS...UNCERTAINTY IN THE LONGEVITY OF THE MID-LEVEL FLOW ENHANCEMENT...COMBINED WITH THE MAIN BELT OF STRONGER FLOW BEING DISPLACED TO THE N OF THE AREA...LIMITS CONFIDENCE IN A THREAT FOR ORGANIZED SVR STORMS. FURTHERMORE...VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGES REVEAL STABLE WAVE CLOUD FORMATIONS OVER THE MOUNTAINS OF FAR NERN TN AND ADJACENT PARTS OF VA/NC INDICATING SOME ONGOING CONVECTIVE INHIBITION. WHILE THIS INHIBITION MAY ERODE DURING THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS OWING TO CONTINUED DIURNAL HEATING...IT COULD ALSO SERVE TO LIMIT STORM/SVR COVERAGE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE AREA IS BEING MONITORED FOR AN INCREASING SVR TSTM POTENTIAL...AND THE ISSUANCE OF A SVR TSTM WATCH IS POSSIBLE ACROSS PARTS OF THE AREA.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A SLOW-MOVING COLD FRONT EXTENDING FROM NERN NEB TO W-CNTRL KS MARKS THE CONTRAST BETWEEN A DEEPLY/WELL-MIXED BOUNDARY LAYER FEATURING HOT SFC TEMPS IN THE MID/UPPER 90S TO 102 DEGREES TO ITS SE...FROM SLIGHTLY COOLER/MORE MOIST CONDITIONS TO ITS NW. HOWEVER...AROUND THE MOIST AXIS CHARACTERIZED BY MIDDLE/UPPER 60S DEWPOINTS NW OF THE COLD FRONT -- AND SOUTHEAST OF A DIFFERENTIAL HEATING ZONE LYING PARALLEL TO...AND 60-75 MILES NW OF...THE COLD FRONT -- CLOUD-FREE AREAS ARE CONTRIBUTING TO MLCAPE UP TO 2000 J/KG PER MODIFIED NORTH PLATTE/OMAHA 12Z RAOBS. VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGES DEPICT ARCS/ZONES OF CUMULUS DEVELOPMENT WITHIN THIS ZONE...WITH HIGHER-BASED CUMULUS DEVELOPMENT CLOSER TO THE COLD FRONT. ISOLATED TO SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO EVOLVE FROM THIS CUMULUS DURING THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS. AND...WITH 20-30 KT OF EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR -- HIGHEST NEAR THE DIFFERENTIAL HEATING ZONE -- MULTICELL CLUSTERS WITH DMGG WIND GUSTS AND PERHAPS SVR HAIL WILL BE OF CONCERN. THESE FACTORS MAY WARRANT SVR TSTM WATCH ISSUANCE ACROSS PARTS OF THE AREA...ESPECIALLY NEAR AND TO THE NORTHEAST OF THE KS/NEB BORDER WHERE THE DIFFERENTIAL HEATING ZONE IS MORE PRONOUNCED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: RAPID CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT MAY OCCUR IN THE NEXT FEW HOURS...WITH A DAMAGING WIND THREAT DEVELOPING. THIS THREAT COULD BECOME ORGANIZED AND MOVE EWD INTO LOWER MI LATER THIS EVENING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SURFACE ANALYSIS SHOWS LOW PRESSURE CENTERED NEAR LSE...WITH TROUGH EXTENDING NWWD NEAR THE MS RIVER. A COLD FRONT WAS MOVING SEWD ACROSS THE MSP AREA...EXTENDING SWWD TOWARD FSD. MEANWHILE...A WARM FRONT CONTINUED TO LIFT NWD ACROSS WI...EXTENDING FROM NEAR MSP TO GRB AT 20Z. STRONG HEATING HAS BEEN OCCURRING ALL DAY ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR...WITH TEMPERATURES OVER 100F INTO SWRN WI. AIRCRAFT SOUNDINGS NEAR MSP INDICATE CAPPING BUT STRONG TCU DEVELOPMENT NE OF LSE SUGGEST CIN IS ERODING THERE. THE CORRIDOR FROM CNTRL WI SWWD ALIGNS WITH THE LOW LEVEL JET AS WELL...WHICH WILL CONTINUE TO PUSH WARM AIR NEWD OVER THE WARM FRONT WITH PRESSURE FALLS NOTED OVER WI. TO THE W...THE COLD FRONT WILL ALSO CONTINUE SEWD...WITH PRESSURE RISES. FORCING OVER THE REGION SHOULD INCREASE AS THE FRONT PROGRESSES SEWD. THE ATMOSPHERE HAS BECOME VERY UNSTABLE AND STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO FORM ACROSS CNTRL WI. WLY DEEP LAYER SHEAR OF 40-45 KT ALONG WITH MODEST LOW LEVEL VEERING WINDS MAY SUPPORT SUPERCELLS INITIALLY...BUT LIKELY TRANSITIONING QUICKLY INTO AN MCS WITH DAMAGING WINDS LIKELY. ONCE FORMED...THIS SYSTEM WOULD LIKELY PERSIST FOR SOME TIME INTO LOWER MI LATER THIS EVENING.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED THREAT FOR SVR THUNDERSTORMS MAY CONDITIONALLY EXIST INTO THE EVENING HOURS. WHILE CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED...WW ISSUANCE IS CURRENTLY UNLIKELY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGES AND SURFACE OBSERVATIONS INDICATE A HOT/DEEPLY-MIXED BOUNDARY LAYER OVERTAKING A WARM SECTOR WHOSE NERN BOUND IS DELINEATED BY A WARM FRONT ARCING FROM NEAR SOUTH BEND IND TO W OF DAYTON OH AND TO E OF JACKSON KY.
